title: Mate with Queen or Rook
concept: Box the king in, shrink the box, bring your own king to help.

glossary.definition: The squares the lone king can still reach. Every good move makes the box smaller, until there's nowhere left.

summary: With a queen or a rook: cut the king off, shrink its box row by row, bring your own king close, and give mate on the edge. Watch out for stalemate: always leave the king a move until you can mate.

narration: Queen and king against a lone king: a win, if you know the method. Squeeze the king to the edge, then bring your own king in to help.
Your king steps up to e7. It isn't just watching: it guards squares the queen can't.
Black's king backs off toward the corner.
Queen to d4. No check, just a smaller box: the long diagonal and the whole 4th row are now out of bounds.
Black's king shuffles to h7. Its box is tiny.
Your king steps to f7, guarding g8, g7 and g6. The black king has one square left.
Off to h6, the last square in the box.
Queen to h4, checkmate! The queen checks along the h-file, and your king covers g6 and g7. Teamwork.

guided.hint: Use the queen to cut the board in two, then shrink the box. Bring your king up before you go for mate.
The rook cuts off a whole row or file. Push the king to the edge, bring your king face to face with it, then check from the side.
